messages.content: Write the copy for the pricing page of a code review tool, covering three tiers. Around 250 words.

**Pricing**

Every plan reviews every pull request. The difference is how much of your codebase the reviewer has actually read, and who picks up the phone when it gets something wrong.

---

**Solo, free**

One developer, public repositories, unlimited reviews. Comments show up on the PR about 90 seconds after you push. No card, no seat count, no expiry date. It won't quietly become an invoice in month two.

---

**Team, $19 per developer per month**

Private repositories and shared review rules. Write your conventions once in a YAML file that lives in your repo rather than in our dashboard, and the reviewer holds everyone to them. It reads your last 500 commits before it opens its mouth, so it stops relitigating decisions your team made years ago. GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket all included. Billing follows active committers: if someone didn't push during a period, they aren't on the bill.

---

**Enterprise, from $12,000 per year**

Everything in Team, plus self-hosted deployment for code that can't leave your network. SSO through SAML or OIDC. Audit logs you can export. A named engineer who answers in Slack, and a 99.9% uptime commitment with money behind it. Volume pricing starts at 40 developers.

---

We don't charge per review, per line, or per token. A team that reviews carefully shouldn't pay more than one that rubber-stamps.

Switching off another tool and want to know what that looks like? Email sales@. A person reads it, usually the same day.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.
